issues.failure_explanation: N_eps takes a supremum over every initialization in Theta, but the proof only gives a bound with constants M_1, M_2 depending on A=f(theta_0)-f*, on B=sum Delta_n(theta_0), and on L=L_f+L_h of a compact set built from the sublevel set at f(theta_0)+T. For unbounded Theta, compact sublevel sets force f to be coercive, so sup over theta_0 of A is infinite. With trust radii summing to about 2 sqrt(n)/log n, far initializations need arbitrarily many steps, so N_eps can be infinite.

issues.failure_explanation: The crossing argument proves divergence of sum ||theta_{t_k+1}-theta_{t_k}|| for the inexact iterates. It then invokes Prop. stationary_conditions, whose hypothesis concerns the exact points theta*_{n_k+1}. Under A3(a) there is no strong convexity, and Prop. parameter_gap_decay only gives ||theta_n - theta*_n||=o(1), each term being up to O(r_n). The difference therefore need not be summable along crossing indices, and divergence for the inexact iterates does not transfer to the exact points.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the assumption sum_n ||theta_n - theta*_n|| < infinity (or exact solves) for the trust-region case. Alternatively, give a new argument transferring divergence from inexact to exact steps.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem (iii) under A3(a) is unproven for inexact sub-problem solutions, which is the regime the paper calls its most technical contribution. Exact computation is unaffected.
issues.title: Asymptotic stationarity with trust region: inexact steps conflated with exact points
issues.why_classification: The conclusion survives under a strengthened inexactness assumption, but the advertised robustness under merely summable optimality gaps is lost for the trust-region variant.

Different from MU and MU-Lin, the updates of MUR is a gradient descent from $\tilde{H}_n$ instead of $H_n$.

issues.failure_explanation: The surrogate is expanded at h_n=H_n^j, so it is tight at H_n. Its minimizer is H_n-(D+rho I)^{-1}grad f(H_n), not the MUR update. The gradient computation and the MUR formula instead expand at H_tilde_n = H_n v delta. The surrogate actually minimized is tight at H_tilde_n, not at the current iterate, so sharpness fails whenever H_n has entries below delta. Either way, MUR does not fit Algorithm 1 and Theorem thm:complexity cannot be invoked. Monotone decrease is also lost, since f(H_tilde_n) may exceed f(H_n).
